newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila millers to buy U.S. wheat on price falls.
newsitem.headline: Manila millers to buy U.S. wheat on price falls.

text.p: Philippine flour millers are expected to go back into the U.S. market next week to buy more wheat if prices fall further from current levels, traders said on Friday.
"I think the U.S. wheat market has reached bottom, and local flour millers realise that now is the time for them to order for nearby shipments," said one Japanese commodity trader.
Local flour millers said they may enter the market if prices fall to interesting levels.
"For now up to the Christmas season, we are fully stocked. But if prices fall to cheap levels we still have room for more stocks," one executive in a local flour mill told Reuters.
Two Philippine firms had asked for price quotations for 28,000 tonnes of western white wheat and dark northern spring wheat on Friday, the traders said.
The price of the December futures contract in Minneapolis, where the Philippines buys most of its wheat, closed U.S. 2-3/4 cents down on Thursday at $4.20 a bushel.

Philippine flour mills on Wednesday bought 19,040 tonnes of western white wheat at US$167-$168 a tonne C&F, 16,000 tonnes of dark northern spring wheat with 13.5 percent protein at $188 a tonne C&F, and 4,960 tonnes of dark northern spring wheat with 14 percent protein at $192.50-$193.00 per tonne, traders said.
The wheat was for end-October to November shipment, one trader said.
Philippine flour mills also bought 41,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat for November delivery on October 4, said one dealer.

The government's Trade and Industry Department said the current retail price of hard flour in Metro Manila rose to 300 pesos per 25 kg from 290 last week while soft flour was steady at 260 pesos per 25 kg.
Hard flour is used in making bread while soft flour is used in making cakes and pastries.

Traders said the average retail price of yellow whole grain corn for feeds dropped to 7.20 pesos a kg from 7.50 pesos while the average retail price of white whole grain corn used in making starch softened to 7.50 pesos from 7.80 pesos.
